analyzer: h1+h2+h3 rubric scoring (agent judgment on collected evidence + measured k6 load + JFR profile under the h2 load window)

buildPasses.note: Clean mvn package on Java 21. NOTE: pom has a malformed lombok scope ('annotationProcessor') — Maven warns it 'threatens the stability of your build' (dependency-analyze.log).

testsPass.note: Suite green (requires external Postgres on localhost:5432 for non-IT tests; ran with practice-postgres up).

testDepth.note: 4 test files, 286 test LOC vs 214 main LOC, but only 8 grep-visible assertion calls across controller/service/integration tests — real but shallow happy-path coverage.

layering.note: controller / service(+impl) / repository / DTOs separation; Caffeine CacheConfig isolated in its own class.

frameworkFit.note: Blocking MVC + Caffeine for simple CRUD — workable and honest for the workload; blocking stack caps concurrency headroom (a runtime question, deferred to h2/h3).

structuralSanity.note: No god classes (max 43 LOC main); violation: hardcoded DB password in application.yaml.

riskBloat.note: Malformed POM model warning (lombok scope) plus starter-transitive used-undeclared noise; no unused-declared bloat beyond false positives.

boots.note: Boots in the docker envelope and serves the full load at both profiles: 0% failed requests, checks 100%.

latencyThroughput.note: PASS at both profiles: p95 170ms / 2168 rps @200 VUs (highest throughput of the set); p95 86ms @50 VUs. Caveat: k6 container has 1 CPU — 2168 rps may approach the generator ceiling, compressing the top end.

jfrProfile.note: One concerning but non-dominant mechanism: 895 monitor events p95 470ms, mostly Tomcat RecycledProcessors at 2133 rps (container-level, not application locks). DB SocketReads 5,524 p95 89ms but amortized: ~2.7x fewer reads/request than its non-caffeine sibling at 2.2x the throughput — the cache verifiably absorbs the read path.

legibility.note: Small, consistent, readable; nonstandard capitalized package segment.

hygiene.note: Two violations: no license file, hardcoded DB password in application.yaml.
